- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model consistently underreacts to sharp price spikes in the prior 3–5 days; add a small lagged correction (e.g., +0.5–1.0 units) to forecast after a spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.2–0.4 units; if below, increase by 0.1–0.3 units.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; apply a “tail correction” — add 0.1–0.3 units to forecast if sentiment is positive and price has been trending upward for 5+ days.
- Avoid forecasting below 65.0 unless sentiment is clearly bearish and price is trending downward; use sentiment as a floor trigger.
